temporalGapMatrix.currentSourceTruth: Each entity exists as exactly one row in districts, parliamentary_constituencies, constituencies. Overwriting attributes destroys history.
temporalGapMatrix.requiredCapability: Model multiple temporal versions of the same entity across distinct statutory or electoral regimes.
temporalGapMatrix.evidence: W013 schema defines UNIQUE(code) on districts and UNIQUE(internal_id) on constituencies with single scalar attributes.
temporalGapMatrix.riskIfNotAddressed: HIGH — Inability to query historical boundaries, past election results in historical constituency definitions, or administrative district splits without data destruction.

temporalGapMatrix.currentSourceTruth: Entities have created_at and updated_at (system audit timestamps only). No statutory or operational validity intervals.
temporalGapMatrix.requiredCapability: Explicit valid_from (DATE NOT NULL) and valid_to (DATE, NULL for active) defining entity lifespan.
temporalGapMatrix.evidence: districts and constituencies contain only TIMESTAMPTZ system timestamps; no calendar validity columns exist.
temporalGapMatrix.riskIfNotAddressed: HIGH — Point-in-time reconstruction is impossible; cannot determine which district or constituency was legally in effect on a given date.

temporalGapMatrix.currentSourceTruth: Tables have zero self-referencing lineage pointers to track entity evolution (splits, mergers, renames, abolitions).
temporalGapMatrix.requiredCapability: Explicit predecessor/successor relationship graph (e.g. entity_lineage or predecessor_entity_id).
temporalGapMatrix.evidence: districts table has no parent_district_id, predecessor_id, or split/merger metadata.
temporalGapMatrix.riskIfNotAddressed: MEDIUM — Users cannot trace how historical entities evolved into present ones (e.g. Warangal split into 5 districts in 2016).

temporalGapMatrix.concept: Relationship Temporality (AC -> District, AC -> PC, Mandal -> District)
temporalGapMatrix.currentSourceTruth: Foreign keys are hardcoded 1:1 or N:1 column references on the child table (e.g. constituencies.district_id).
temporalGapMatrix.requiredCapability: Temporal relationship mapping. When administrative districts split, electoral ACs remain unchanged but their parent district mapping changes over time.
temporalGapMatrix.evidence: constituencies.district_id is a single static UUID foreign key.
temporalGapMatrix.riskIfNotAddressed: CRITICAL — Reorganizing administrative districts forces destructive updates to constituencies.district_id, corrupting historical electoral reports.

temporalGapMatrix.currentSourceTruth: delimitation_proposals exists in DDL with status in ('draft', 'final', 'superseded', 'rejected'), but has no formal linkage to W012 provenance or canonical entities.
temporalGapMatrix.requiredCapability: Strict architectural barrier preventing hypothetical delimitation simulations from polluting canonical tables or being marked OFFICIAL.
temporalGapMatrix.evidence: 011_delimitation.sql proposed_constituencies table uses integer new_ac_no without canonical UUID or W012 governance checks.
temporalGapMatrix.riskIfNotAddressed: HIGH — Contamination of official public geography by unnotified draft delimitation proposals.

datasetVersionVsEntityVersion.datasetVersion: W012 concept: Represents an ingested source package (e.g. eci_ts_ac_2008_v1, published by ECI in 2008).
datasetVersionVsEntityVersion.entityVersion: W014 concept: Represents a specific statutory/electoral manifestation of an entity during a real-world time interval.
datasetVersionVsEntityVersion.cardinality: N:M or N:1. A single dataset version can publish attributes for multiple entity versions, and a long-lived entity version may be re-affirmed across multiple dataset releases.

defectsIdentified.title: Flat Geography Schema vs Versioned Delimitation Graph
defectsIdentified.status: IN_PROGRESS (Quarantined to W013–W017; W014 preflight addresses core temporal graph)
defectsIdentified.disposition: W014 will design the temporal entity and relationship versioning schema to resolve the temporal dimension of DEF-006.
